title: Orchestration, Fidelity Fences, and Safety Contracts for Kernel Rollouts
author: Sophie Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the operational contracts, safety fences, and validation procedures used when rolling out new kernel codepaths, scheduler policies, or execution-time optimizations into the Redwood serving runtime. It focuses on preserving customer-facing SLOs, preventing fidelity regressions, and enabling deterministic rollback.

Scope: kernel patches, scheduling policy updates, kernel selection heuristics, quantization-aware execution paths, and any runtime change that alters the token emission path. Not in scope: model weights, client SDK changes, or unrelated infra (network/storage) updates.

Audience: runtime engineers, SREs, release engineers, and applied ML owners who approve model-serving risk.

Key Concepts and Definitions

- Fidelity fence: a runtime-enforced boundary that keeps inference outputs within an acceptable quality envelope during transient kernel transitions (e.g., preserving top-k behavior, temperature semantics, or deterministic sampling seeds).
- Kernel handshake: a short protocol (telemetry + state exchange) between scheduler and GPU dispatcher to confirm compatibility and resource accounting before activation.
- Stitching window: the safe timeframe after a kernel switch where additional telemetry is collected (higher sampling rate) and aggressive fallbacks are enabled.
- Contract version: semantic version tag for kernel behaviour guarantees (e.g., v1.2.0-contract-A) used in rollouts and tracing.

Operational Contracts (must be satisfied before rollout)

1) Observability contract
   - All kernel releases must emit the following telemetry keys at INFO level: kernel.contract_version, kernel.handshake_latency_ms, kernel.activation_slot_id, kernel.fidelity_score_delta, kernel.fallback_trigger.
   - Traces must include a correlation id (request.trace_id) and kernel.contract_version for every request that touches the new codepath.

2) SLO preservation contract
   - For any target model route, new kernels must demonstrate no more than +5% p99 latency and no more than +3% failure rate in canary traffic vs baseline.
   - Fidelity regressions must be bounded: automated eval harness score delta <= configured threshold for that model route (see per-route fidelity thresholds).

3) Rollback determinism contract
   - A rollback path that restores previous contract_version must preserve kvcache consistency or declare a cache flush procedure. Rollbacks must complete within the configured rollback_timeout (default 90s).

4) Resource accounting contract
   - Kernel handshake must expose the kernel.resource_profile annotated with memory_peak_bytes, scratch_gpu_bytes, and compute_wave_estimate. Admission controller uses these to avoid overcommit.

Validation and Canary Procedure (step-by-step)

1) Preflight (local lab)
   - Run unit + microbench: ./tooling/kernel-bench --kernel candidate.so --sequence-lengths 32,256 --concurrency 1,8
   - Produce deterministic trace for a small corpus (use: test-corpus/fidelity-critical.jsonl).

2) Canary experiment (staging cluster)
   - Stage: deploy with kernel.contract_version set to candidate tag and the following release flags: --canary-weight=5 --stitching-window=300s --telemetry-sampling=100
   - Monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rates, kernel.fidelity_score_delta, user-visible metric (per-route BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-cosine).

3) Automated gating
   - If any of these triggers fire, the system will auto-fail the canary and initiate rollback:
     a) p99 latency increase > 5% for 10 consecutive minutes
     b) request failure-rate delta > 3% vs baseline for 5 minutes
     c) fidelity_score_delta > per-route-threshold for 1 minute
     d) kernel.handshake_latency_ms > 1s for any activation

4) Gradual ramp
   - Ramp weights: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with a minimum observation window of 15 minutes and metric stability check after each step.

Validation Checklist (table)

| Item | Requirement | Owner | Pass criteria |
|------|-------------|-------|---------------|
| Unit tests | Kernel unit-suite + scheduler compat tests | Author | All green on CI |
| Perf microbench | Throughput & latency baseline | Perf owner | p99 <= +5% |
| Fidelity eval | Eval harness run vs golden prompts | ML owner | score delta <= threshold |
| Handshake telemetry | Contract fields present | Runtime SRE | Verified in traces |
| Chaos dry-run | Simulated GPU eviction and kernel fallback | SRE | Recovery within rollback_timeout |

(When rendered in Confluence, the above table should be a proper table. The stored JSON keeps ASCII table for searchability.)

Safeguards and Automation

- Safety tripwires: Per-cluster admission controller rejects activation of candidate kernels if aggregate memory_reservation + candidate.resource_profile.memory_peak_bytes > 0.95 * cluster_memory_budget.
- Circuit breaker: If fallback_trigger fires more than 3 times in 1 minute across a shard group, that kernel version gets blacklisted for that shard group and remains in canary with 0% weight until manually approved.
- Automatic KVCACHE reconciliation: When a rollback is initiated, a controlled cache drain occurs for affected sessions with the following CLI: 

  # drain keys gracefully for a model route
  redwoodctl cache drain --route product-recommendations --timeout 60s --mode graceful

Benchmarking and Profiling Integration

- Kernel microbench harness example (YAML):

  benchmarks:
    - name: small-context-latency
      seq_len: 32
      batch_shapes: [[1],[4]]
      concurrency: 1
    - name: long-context-throughput
      seq_len: 1024
      batch_shapes: [[1,16],[2,8]]
      concurrency: 8

  validation:
    fidelity_corpus: test-corpus/fidelity-critical.jsonl
    baseline_trace: traces/baseline-v1.1.jsonl

- Example command to run an annotated profile and push to observability: 

  ./tooling/kernel-bench --config=bench/kernel-ci.yaml --profile=perftrace --push-to=kusto --tag=candidate-2026-01

- Profiling guidance: prioritize wandb-style sample IDs correlating kernel.handshake events with GPU SM counters. Collect top-down breakdown: scheduler_queue_ms, kernel_launch_ms, kernel_exec_ms, memcpy_ms.

Runbook: Kernel-induced Latency Surge (operational playbook)

1) Detection
   - Alert: runtime.kernel.p99_delta > +5% AND rate(5xx) increased

2) Immediate actions (0-2 minutes)
   - Identify recent kernel.contract_version activations via trace query:

     query: traces | where kernel.contract_version != "stable" | summarize count() by kernel.contract_version, shard_group

   - If suspect contract_version found, execute controlled canary rollback: redwoodctl rollout rollback --contract <tag> --scope cluster:canary

3) Short-term remediation (2-15 minutes)
   - Engage perf on-call; increase telemetry sampling to 100% for affected routes: redwoodctl telemetry set-sampling --route <route> --rate 100
   - Run targeted microbench on the staging copy of the shard (see Benchmarking section).

4) Post-incident (15+ minutes)
   - Produce timeline: include handshake_latency_ms, fallback_trigger counts, stitch-window duration, and kvcache-miss rates.
   - Decide: revert and iterate, or patch and re-canary.

Chaos and Validation Experiments (recommended patterns)

- Eviction storm: simulate 10% random GPU evictions during canary to verify fallback correctness. Expected behaviour: fallback_trigger increased briefly; p99 remains < +8% and rollback_timeout not exceeded.
- Kernel handshake timeouts: inject artificial 2s latency to kernel.handshake and verify admission controller blocks new activations.
- Cross-tenant pressure: run a mixed workload where priority-synthetic traffic competes for memory; ensure tenant-aware resource_profile admission rejects candidate if headroom < 5%.

Metrics and Dashboards to Monitor

- runtime.kernel.contract_version (tag)
- kernel.handshake_latency_ms (histogram)
- kernel.fidelity_score_delta (gauge, per-route)
- kernel.fallback_trigger (counter)
- request.latency.{p50,p95,p99} (by route and contract_version)
- kvcache.hit_rate (per-session)

Example Dashboard Widgets

1) Rollout summary: heatmap of p99 delta by contract_version and route.
2) Handshake latency histogram with alarm band at 1s.
3) Fidelity scatter: fidelity_score_delta vs latency delta per sample (helps detect tradeoffs).

Ownership, Approvals, and Release Notes Requirements

- Owners: kernel author (code), runtime SRE (rollout), applied ML owner (fidelity thresholds).
- Approvals required: code review, perf sign-off, ML sign-off (if route is customer-facing), security scan clearance.
- Release note template (short):

  - Title: kernel update <contract_version>
  - Summary: short description of optimization and intended effect
  - Risk: list of routes impacted and fidelity gates
  - Rollout plan: canary weights and ramp windows
  - Contact: primary author + on-call SRE

Appendix: Useful queries and commands

- Trace query: traces | where kernel.contract_version == "candidate-2026-01" | summarize count() by outcome_code
- blacklisting a kernel for a shard group: redwoodctl kernel blacklist --contract candidate-2026-01 --shard-group shard-17 --reason "fallback-rate-high"
- run local synthetic evaluation: ./tooling/eval-harness --model-route product-recommendations --input test-corpus/fidelity-critical.jsonl --compare traces/baseline-v1.1.jsonl
